_meta.indication: Treatment of acute uncomplicated influenza in patients 18 years and older who have been symptomatic for no more than 2 days

pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, dose-finding trial of a single IV dose (peramivir 300 mg, 600 mg, or placebo) administered over 30 minutes, conducted in Japan
pivotal_trials.population: Subjects 18 to 65 years of age with acute uncomplicated influenza (fever greater than 38°C and positive rapid antigen test), symptomatic no more than 48 hours
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint: time to alleviation of symptoms – hours from initiation of study drug until all seven influenza symptoms were absent or no greater than mild for at least 21.5 hours
pivotal_trials.n: N=300 enrolled; efficacy population 297 with confirmed influenza (300 mg: 99 randomized/99 treated; 600 mg: 100 randomized/99 treated; placebo: 101 randomized/100 treated)
pivotal_trials.result: Peramivir 600 mg reduced median time to alleviation of symptoms by ~22 hours vs placebo (median healing 59.9 vs 81.8 hrs; HR 0.666, 95% limits 0.499–0.89; P=0.0046)

key_safety: Most common adverse reaction (incidence >2%) was diarrhea, 8% with RAPIVAB 600 mg versus 7% placebo; no serious adverse event and <1% discontinued. Warnings: serious skin/hypersensitivity reactions (Stevens-Johnson syndrome, erythema multiforme) and neuropsychiatric events
target_moa: Peramivir is an inhibitor of influenza virus neuraminidase, an enzyme that releases viral particles from the plasma membrane of infected cells

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting was held; review of the application did not warrant convening an Advisory Committee Meeting as peramivir is not a first-in-class drug and there is ample clinical experience with other NAI drugs

description.text: Expanded treatment of acute uncomplicated influenza to pediatric patients 6 months and older symptomatic for no more than two days

citations.quote: - Expands the patient population of Rapivab (peramivir) for the treatment of acute uncomplicated influenza to patients 6 months and older who have been symptomatic for no more than two days.

summary.text: RAPIVAB NDA 206426 was submitted December 23, 2013 and reviewed under the PDUFA V program with a goal date of December 24, 2014; approval was based primarily on the Phase 2 Study 0722T0621. No advisory committee was convened as peramivir is not a first-in-class drug and there is ample clinical experience with other NAI drugs.

citations.quote: The NDA for the peramivir was submitted on December 23, 2013 and reviewed under the PDUFA V program.

Date of Submission	December 23, 2013
